instruction:
Fix `packages/element/src/textRanges.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 security findings 1 and 2 (security_review.md), accepted by the user. (1) Medium, SVG injection: isValidRangeColor (line 17) accepts any non-empty string other than 'transparent', so crafted scene/collab payloads can put url(...) paint-server references or oversized strings into <rect fill>/<tspan fill> on SVG export and into editable.dataset.textRanges. Restrict it to bounded CSS colour tokens only: hex #rgb/#rgba/#rrggbb/#rrggbbaa; rgb()/rgba()/hsl()/hsla() with only digits, '.', '%', ',', '/', spaces and optional 'deg' inside the parentheses; or an ASCII-letters-only named colour; total length at most 64 characters after trim; reject 'transparent', url(...), and anything else. Keep the signature `(color: unknown): color is string`. (2) Medium, DoS: normalizeTextRanges (line 25) processes an unbounded ranges array with an O(N^2) loop, and getStyleForTextRange (line ~374) calls `Math.max(end, ...ranges.map((r) => r.end))`, which can overflow the call stack. Add and export `export const MAX_TEXT_RANGES = 512;` and in normalizeTextRanges inspect only the first MAX_TEXT_RANGES entries of the input array; in getStyleForTextRange compute the maximum end with a for loop instead of the spread. Change nothing else; every existing test must still pass.

Anchoring: make exactly two edits, each with a unique search text. (a) Add `import { actionChangeStrokeColor } from "../actions/actionProperties";` next to an existing unique import line. Do NOT import actionChangeHighlightColor: it is deleted this round. (b) Search for the unique line `      expect(h.elements.filter((el) => !el.isDeleted)).toHaveLength(0);` (it appears once, inside it("removes a plain text in a single undo")) and replace it with itself + `\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe("per-range text styling", () => {` + the new cases, so that the file's remaining `    });\n  });\n});` closes the last new it(), the new describe and the outer describe. In every case, create the text element with API.createElement({ type: "text", text: "Hello world", ... }) and put it in the scene (API.setElements / as the file's existing-element tests do), then open the editor on it (Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER) with it selected, or a double-click, as existing tests do). Never use the text tool. Set the selection explicitly (editor.selectionStart/selectionEnd). Apply colour with h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { currentItemStrokeColor: "#e03131" }) and highlight with h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { highlightColor: "#ffec99" }). Cases: (1) live display, which passed before: with selection 0..5, apply the colour and the highlight, then, with h.state.editingTextElement still set, assert editor.style.color === "transparent", JSON.parse(editor.dataset.textRanges!) holds the range, and h.app.renderer.getRenderableElements(...).elementsMap.get(id)?.textRanges holds it; (2) live typing shifts and deletes ranges, which passed before; (3) a collapsed selection (selectionStart === selectionEnd) recolours the whole element's strokeColor and leaves no 'textRanges' own property, which passed before; (4) undo/redo: on an existing element, styling during the edit is its own undo entry (captured IMMEDIATELY). Apply the highlight to 0..5, exit the editor (Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor)), assert textRanges is set, then call Keyboard.undo() once: textRanges must be undefined and 'textRanges' in el must be false.
